extracted.intended_audience: general readers, media researchers, journalists interested in BBC controversies and editorial standards
extracted.subtask_description: Summarises criticisms and implied standards for BBC news and documentary output, focusing on impartiality, accuracy, regional representation, and organisational practices. Useful for evaluating BBC coverage or for people studying broadcaster editorial standards and controversies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity about the geographic scope of 'UK-wide' news
rubrics_metrics.description: The flagship newscasts are based in London and tend to report 'nation-wide' stories related to government and policy that often pertain only England or sometimes England and Wales.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial output should make clear when a story applies only to a constituent nation (example: explain that the Junior Doctors Strike affected only England or that Scotland and Northern Ireland are exempt from the bedroom tax). Lack of clarity creates additional responsibility for home nations to report on devolved matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibility and accountability to devolved bodies
rubrics_metrics.description: From 2016, BBC management would go before the devolved committees for culture or media to answer questions and criticism, just as for the Westminster Culture, Media, and Sport Committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The corporation should accept scrutiny and answer devolved parliaments'/media committees about coverage of regional/devolved matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequate regional focus (e.g., Wales)
rubrics_metrics.description: Criticism that there is a lack of a Welsh focus on BBC news broadcasts and frustration over how the Welsh Assembly is characterised in national media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: News broadcasts should provide thorough, proportionate coverage of constituent nations and avoid marginalising devolved institutions; failures may provoke public frustration and political pressure (examples: threats to withhold licence fees).

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartiality and balanced coverage in referendum and political campaigns
rubrics_metrics.description: Accusations that BBC coverage of the Scotland independence referendum was biased towards the unionist No campaign; questions raised about costs being 'downplayed' and unequal treatment of political viewpoints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Political debates, referendums and campaigns must be covered impartially, giving appropriate and proportionate airtime and scrutiny to relevant positions and figures. Appointments and promotions (e.g., presenters with partisan links) and facilitation of campaign advertising can be perceived as breaches of editorial guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal visibility for significant political actors
rubrics_metrics.description: Concerns that balance predicated on party-political bases can ignore significant political voices relevant to a yes/no question (example: Patrick Harvie of the Scottish Greens receiving less coverage than national party leaders).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial judgment about balance should consider the nature of the question (e.g., yes/no referendum) and ensure significant actors receive coverage proportionate to their relevance to that issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of presenter or staff partiality on air
rubrics_metrics.description: Instances where presenters (or former staff) were accused of expressing political views or where interviews were criticised for apparent partiality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presenters should avoid expressing unqualified political opinions on air; interview conduct must uphold impartiality standards and editorial guidance. Apparent partiality can trigger complaints and calls for inquiry or dismissal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precision and qualification in professional statements
rubrics_metrics.description: The editorial standards committee found a radio piece 'had stated his professional view without qualification or explanation, and that the lack of precision in his language had rendered the statement inaccurate.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists must use precise, qualified language when expressing professional opinions; lack of precision can make content inaccurate and breach impartiality rules. Online articles should explain the existence of alternative views where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to explain alternative views in reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: The committee said an online article should have explained the existence of alternative views and that omission breached impartiality rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where matters are contested, reporting should make clear competing perspectives rather than presenting a single view as uncontested fact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification of footage and avoidance of fake material
rubrics_metrics.description: Panorama report on Primark included footage that was probably fake; the BBC apologised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Producers must verify the provenance and authenticity of video/footage used in reports; failure can require public apology and damage credibility and sources' reputations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of sensationalism and responsible local reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Coverage that suggested a child was questioned over anti-terrorism because he wrote 'terrorist house' was criticised as sensationalised and untrue; police said the reporter was aware it was not a terror incident.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Local stories should not be sensationalised; reporters must understand and communicate the factual context and potential impact on communities, avoiding headlines or framing that exaggerates or misrepresents events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of one-sided or exploitative documentaries
rubrics_metrics.description: Euro 2012: Stadiums of Hate was accused of being one-sided, biased and unethical; sources said they were exploited and a false horror story was concocted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documentaries should present balanced evidence, avoid selective sourcing or manipulation, and not exploit interviewees to manufacture sensational narratives; ethical sourcing practices and context are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of false claims, libel and defamation
rubrics_metrics.description: BBC agreed to pay damages to Petro Poroshenko after publishing libellous reports; Gerry Adams won damages where the BBC was found not to have acted in good faith.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure rigorous fact-checking of potentially defamatory allegations, corroborate anonymous sourcing, and act in 'good faith' and a 'fair and reasonable' way to minimise legal risk and harm to reputation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of stereotyping and simplistic portrayals of countries/cultures
rubrics_metrics.description: Research found many BBC documentaries on China used largely negative language, portrayed culture simplistically and enabled stereotypes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coverage of foreign countries should avoid reductive or negative stereotyping, provide cultural context, and resist simplistic framing that reinforces prejudices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency and transparency across language versions and edits
rubrics_metrics.description: Accusations arose from perceived differences between English and Chinese-language versions of a Wuhan video, and debate about changes in coloration between versions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When producing content for different language audiences, editorial teams should ensure consistency or transparently explain differences; discrepancies can fuel claims of bias or manipulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proportionate application of impartiality in science reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: A review found an 'over-rigid' application of editorial guidelines on impartiality in relation to science coverage, failing to consider the 'non-contentious' nature of some stories and the need to avoid giving 'undue attention to marginal opinion' (examples: MMR vaccine, GM crops, man-made climate change).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial standards should reflect the scientific consensus where appropriate; impartiality does not require presenting fringe denials as equivalent to well-supported science—avoid false balance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not platform outright denial as equal counterpoint in settled matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Internal notice: 'Manmade climate change exists: If the science proves it we should report it.... To achieve impartiality, you do not need to include outright deniers of climate change in BBC coverage.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For issues with strong expert consensus, coverage should not routinely include explicit deniers as if they are equivalent authoritative voices; challenge false or misleading claims with factual context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsible use of resources and staffing for coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Criticism for 'overstaffing' news, sporting and cultural events, wasting licence fee money and using dominant position to control event coverage (examples: large numbers sent to Glastonbury, Olympics-related events).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: News organisations should justify deployment of staff against public-service value and cost, avoiding unnecessary overstaffing that wastes public funds or distorts coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and propriety in contract and tax arrangements
rubrics_metrics.description: Public Accounts Committee found many 'off payroll' contracts that enable people to make their own tax arrangements; the BBC said many were short-term but reviewed arrangements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain transparent, legally compliant contracting practices and review off-payroll arrangements to avoid perceptions of tax avoidance or unfair employment practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to diversity, equal opportunities and handling of discrimination complaints
rubrics_metrics.description: References to policy on diversity and equal opportunities and multiple public accusations of institutional racism, homophobia, transphobia and antisemitism; staff complaints and public criticism ensued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The organisation should implement and enforce robust diversity and equal-opportunity policies, address discrimination complaints seriously, and ensure editorial and HR practices do not institutionalise bias. Public perception of institutional discrimination damages credibility.
